tags.feature: Update 1.6 is live, and with it arrives one of our most anticipated features: New Game+.

But Update 1.6 carries more than challenge alone. It also introduces new weapons, major quality-of-life improvements, reworked enemy encounters, smoother combat, polished visuals, and a host of bug fixes.
Brace yourself for the ultimate trial. With New Game+, you can now restart your journey using your battle-hardened Inquisitor and progress through as many NG+ cycles as you dare.
NG+ versions of weapons, off-hands, and rings can now be found to upgrade your arsenal.
Random empowered auras and effects will appear on enemies, offering both greater danger and greater rewards.
New Weapons Added: Aurora (Mid-game Daggers), Crimson Slicer (Late-game Daggers), and Reignbreaker (Late-game Two-Handed Mace).
Added a feature that allows players to remove Skill Upgrades and refund their cost at the Witch Altar.
Individual Talents and Nodes can now be unlearned and refunded at the Witch Altar.
Added an option to instantly learn Talents and Nodes with a single button press.
Vendor items now display a small icon to indicate if they are not yet unlocked in your Collection.
Added Quick Buy/Sell to the General tab of the Options window.
From now on, your Character will only let go of ledges and walls when taking heavy damage.
When using Jump Pads in Entropy, your Inquisitor will now transform into their energy form for the duration of the jump.
Added particle effects to movable boxes.
Added missing visual effect to Step Into the Sunlight quest.
Inactive Skill Set’s resource bars now appear on the HUD.
Ranks (1-3 stars) have been added to enemy unlocks in the Bestiary list.
Statistics page now shows collected Diagrams by vendor type.

tags.balance_change: Difficulty will continue to scale for the first 10, each one more punishing than the last.
Enemies grow tougher with every cycle, scaling their strength to match your power.
Increased Witch Stone selection radius when the Map view is zoomed out.
Glide can now be activated during a later phase of the jump/fall.
Glide's auto-cancel height has been lowered to reduce events where Glide gets cancelled by unintended early landing.
Increased the time window for grabbing ledges and ladders during falls.
You can now turn around during Heavy Attack wind-up.
Sprint and Roll no longer consume Stamina in Tombstone Hollows.
Controller vibration fine-tuned across various attacks.
Dark Ale has been updated with better balance, rewards, and gameplay improvements.
Increased rewards for the following secondary quests:
Nightshade’s Shadowstep reach increased to match its particle effect.
Vanguard’s Eternal Rage Talent now activates at a consistent flat Adrenaline value (100).
Added Spirit scaling to the stagger effect of the Vindicator's Astral Guardians skill.
The damage increase from the Vanguard’s Revenge Talent now also applies to Shield Charge.
Light Attacks with Daggers now generate Adrenaline.
Adjusted Sleepwalker Phase 2 difficulty and removed unavoidable damage events.
Updated Sleepwalker ability hitboxes and preparation times to improve the fight.
Tweaked a mechanic in Phase 2 of the Final Boss fight that required players to stand still to trigger the homing orbs' explosion.
Adjusted the Phase 2 beam contact damage area in the Final Boss fight to better match the visuals.
Updated Lord Auberon's Phase 2 light area visuals to better understand how to avoid taking damage.
Increased the distance between fissures created by the Entropic Forest Giant.
Slight balance adjustment to enemy placement in Lochmuir Village.
A number of Small Spike Pits are now non-lethal and shallower — you can jump out!
Adjusted the facing direction when looking at NPCs.
Air Attack animations improved.
Numerous tweaks to character and cutscene animations.
Polished visual effects in:
Small to medium updates to a number of enemy animations.
Visual improvements to weapon trail effects.
Updated the visual effect for the Entropy Portal.
Tweaked node navigation in the Witch Lantern upgrades window at the Witch Altar.
Tweaked node navigation in the Skill Upgrade screen.
Various item icons received a visual polish pass.
Adjusted margins in Character Creator for localization.
Changed a misleading Perished message when failing in the Dreamfields. In this case, the Inquisitor falls into eternal slumber.

Fixed Weapon Oil effects incorrectly scaling with main attributes.

Fixed an issue that caused the Blood Eye model to sometimes not behave properly when killed.

notes.title: 1.4 Patch Notes - Mandragora: Whispers of the Witch Tree
notes.content:
Inquisitors,

We’ve just released a major update for Mandragora: Whispers of the Witch Tree — Patch 1.4! This huge patch includes plenty of fixes, rebalancing, updated difficulty sliders, Entropy adjustments, and good news for Rhys fans.

Thank you so much if you’ve taken the time to share your feedback — we’re always listening, and we’ve got more updates on the way, so please stay tuned!

[h2]New: Difficulty Modifiers & Additional Checkpoints[/h2]

[b]Difficulty Modifiers[/b]
[list]
[*] Enemy Health and Enemy Damage difficulty settings can now be adjusted between 40% and 160% (compared to the previous range of 70% to 100%). This modifier can be accessed via Accessibility (Options).
[*] Stamina Cost difficulty settings can now be adjusted between 40% and 100% (compared to the previous minimum of 70%). This modifier can be accessed via Accessibility (Options).
[/list]
[b]Characters[/b]
[list]
[*] Rhys is back for everyone and can no longer leave.
[/list]
[b]Navigation[/b]
[list]
[*] New Witch Stones have been added to the following areas: Gloomroot Woods Mining Outpost, Forsaken Mine Vertical Shafts (before the boss), and before the final boss.
[*] After reaching the boss in a Rift, a shortcut portal will become available at the start of the Rift, allowing direct access to the boss.
[*] Players now respawn inside the Entropy Corridor instead of outside the entrance to prevent double loading screens.
[*] A new shortcut is available to the Theater Witch Stone before the Marionettes boss fight.
[*] A new shortcut has been added to the Tome Mistress boss fight.
[/list]
[h2]Game Improvements & Balance Changes[/h2]

[b]Bosses, Enemies & Hazards[/b]

notes.title: Important Update on Data Collection and Privacy removal
notes.content:
Dear Inquisitors,

We want to stress that you, Players, are our first priority. Your trust and the game are at the center of our attention.

Similar to the removal of additional DRM solutions from the game prior to release, which we decided to do after receiving the community feedback and understanding the concerns regarding an unrestricted gaming experience. Allow us now to address your concerns regarding telemetry and data collection in the game.

[h3]What Happened[/h3]

Data collection and telemetry in-game are industry practices that publishers and developers adopt to improve their games (e.g. improve balance, game progression, content, crashes, etc.) - and this was the case too for Mandragora. 

However, we understand that sharing our general-purpose set of legal agreements, including the Privacy Policy, that covers and regulates many different services - including, for example, websites and marketplaces, and many types of games, including multiplayer ones - created only misunderstanding and concerns, instead of fulfilling their key role of giving you maximum transparency. 

[h3]What We’re Doing About It[/h3]

We want you to enjoy the game with peace of mind. For this reason, we have decided to [b]remove all telemetry and data collection from Mandragora, effective immediately.[/b] This will give you a [b]fully offline experience without any information transferred or collected[/b], so you can enjoy the game as you want.

We want to inform you upfront that this change required us to update the EULA removing any unneeded reference to data that is not collected anymore and the references to the now removed Privacy Policy. This requires a patch and you might be asked to accept the new and simplified EULA.

[h3]A patch is already available that removes telemetry from the game![/h3]

For those among you who have previously accepted the Privacy Policy, we want to reassure you:
[list]
[*]We never sold your data nor shared with anyone outside our internal telemetry systems. We are fully compliant with all data protection laws. 
[*]With patch 1.2.7 for Steam, no data will be collected at all, even if you had previously accepted the privacy policy. 
[/list]

If you remain concerned, you can immediately request erasure of data we might have collected, in line with data protection laws. To do this, please reach out to our data protection officer dpo@my.games and mention “Mandragora Privacy Policy” to help us expedite your request.
This will no longer be necessary after patch 1.2.7, as we will no longer be collecting data.

We are also aware that some players have mistakenly seen a connection to our telemetry systems and  would like to take this occasion and confirm that “false positive” Anti-Virus issues (like Windows Defender) are completely unrelated. We have submitted these issues already to the respective third parties companies and hope to get this sorted soon.


[b]We are here to relieve any concerns you might have[/b]

We remain at your disposal should you have any additional questions please feel free to reach us at [b]mandragora@knightspeak.com[/b].



We hope this has solved some of your concerns and you keep enjoying Mandragora.

Thank you for your understanding and continued support.
Team Knights Peak

notes.title: Game Preview 2 Out Now: Experience a New Class, Features, Bosses & More!
notes.content:
[b]If you pre-purchased [i]Mandragora: Whispers of the Witch Tree[/i], we have good news: Game Preview 2 is now available to download and play![/b]

[i]Game Preview 2 is an update to the existing Mandragora Playtest application. Just update the Mandragora Playtest app which is already in your library if you have pre-purchased the game, and you’re ready to go![/i]

I’m Gábor Szabó, Lead Game Designer at Primal Game Studio. I’m excited to tell you that the [i]Mandragora: Whispers of the Witch Tree[/i] Game Preview 2 update is now live. I’m here to give you some more details about it.

Since the launch of Game Preview 1, you’ve sent us a lot of feedback. You shared your enthusiasm about the game, told us what you liked most about it, and also pointed out a couple of things you’d like to see changed. We've carefully considered all feedback, treating each as equally important, and in Game Preview 2, you'll notice many changes and additions based on these insights.

Hundreds of bugs have been fixed, the [b]UI[/b] has been made more user-friendly and streamlined, the [b]air attack[/b] has been completely reworked, [b]Classes[/b] and caravan [b]NPCs[/b] have been rebalanced, many of the Skills have been adjusted, game performance has been drastically improved… and much more.

Game Preview 2 is a major step towards the full release of the game, but our work doesn’t stop here. We still have a lot to do before April 17, and we can’t wait to hear what you think about Preview 2. We're actively developing a major user interface and onboarding update set to launch with the game. And while the current version is already playable, I'm pleased to confirm that the full release will feature [b]full Steam Deck support[/b], including new, small-screen exclusive UI and adjusted visual settings.

Due to the extreme amount of changes to the game since Preview 1, Game Preview 2 is [b]not[/b] compatible with previous save games. But don’t worry, Preview 2 contains so much new content you won't regret taking a fresh look at the early game.

Speaking of new content, depending on your playstyle, Game Preview 2 adds about 3–4 hours of new gameplay compared to Preview 1. That leaves you with a total playtime of 8–9 hours for Game Preview 2—which covers about a quarter of the full story, without even accounting for time spent on other gameplay features.

Here’s a quick look at what exciting new content you can expect with this update.

[h3]Explore more of the story[/h3]

We've talked a lot about how happy we are with the rich narrative we've crafted together with Brian Mitsoda. With this new update, we're thrilled to share even more of that with you.

While Preview 1 already gave you a taste, Game Preview 2 introduces an even more immersive experience, featuring a greater variety of NPCs to interact with, new quests that expand the lore, and fresh areas to explore, each filled with secrets to uncover. In fact, the map of Preview 2 is about 33% bigger than the one you journeyed through in Game Preview 1, so there will be plenty more areas for you to explore and secrets for you to uncover!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41934946/1d5b88e0a81415f301e4288faa544c0efe51f60e.png[/img]

Face off against new Bosses & Enemies
In Preview 1, you had the chance to face off against plenty of tough bosses and minibosses, ranging from the furry to the furious.

Now, in Preview 2, you’ll be able to flex your combat skills against two more challenging bosses and four more minibosses. While we don’t want to spoil too much by revealing their identities, let’s just say you should definitely stock up on health flasks and make sure your sword is sharp enough for the challenge.

[h3]Play as a new Class: Nightshade[/h3]

Having played Game Preview 1, you’ve likely already familiarized yourself with the Vanguard and Spellbinder Classes. Preview 2 introduces a third option: Nightshade.

“This special branch of the Inquisitors undergoes rigorous training to become swift and lethal operatives, executing missions to silently eliminate powerful adversaries who oppose the King Priest.”

That’s really just a fancy way of saying that this Class is perfect for anyone who wants to swiftly eliminate enemies with poison and dual-wield daggers. If you like playing as an assassin in other games, this is the Class for you.

We hope you have fun exploring the Nightshade Class and all its cool abilities—as well as its unique, branching Talent Tree!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41934946/d5acb8f1d4260d43ef8c92cfafc3bbb756cacc47.png[/img]

[h3]Accessibility and Difficulty[/h3]

There's one more topic we believe deserves special attention. Our goal has always been to make Mandragora accessible to as many players as possible. While the game is primarily an action RPG, it is also a challenging experience with many Soulslike elements that seasoned players expect and enjoy from the genre.

However, we recognize that this level of difficulty may not suit everyone for various reasons. To ensure more players can enjoy the game, we’re introducing the first set of our new Accessibility and Difficulty settings, with more accessibility options to come in the future.

This includes three adjustable modifiers: Enemy Health, Enemy Damage, and Skill Stamina Cost, each of which can be customized to 100%, 90%, 80%, or 70%.

These settings can be adjusted not only during character creation but also at any point in the game. So if a particular section feels too difficult, you can tweak the settings just for a tough boss fight and revert them afterward.

We believe these changes will make [i]Mandragora[/i] more enjoyable for a wider audience, and we look forward to hearing your feedback.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41934946/45f2cfd9e54ec1ce34c96fe8e8bffe4744cef251.jpg[/img]

Thank you for being alongside us for this exciting journey - we look forward to seeing you all in Faelduum very soon!

Pre-purchase today to get immediate access to Game Preview 2, alongside many other perks and rewards: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1721060/view/526461085948051463
